title: Public speaking and speech training for CTOs
objectives: Deliver a clear and confident technical talk
Control pace, voice and body language
Adapt a message to different audiences
verificationNotes: Speaking advice is general; practise with real audiences.

sections.heading: Message first
sections.body: A talk needs one central message. Every section should support it. If you cannot state the message in one sentence, the talk is not ready. Audiences remember the message and one or two stories, not the detail.

sections.heading: Voice and pace
sections.body: Speak slower than feels natural. Pause after key points. Vary volume and pitch to signal importance. Avoid filler words by pausing instead. A microphone amplifies speed as much as volume, so slow down further on stage.

sections.heading: Body language
sections.body: Stand still with purpose. Use open gestures. Make eye contact with different parts of the room. Avoid pacing or reading from slides. Your posture should match the confidence of the message.

sections.heading: Audience and questions
sections.body: Adapt depth to the audience. Engineers want mechanisms and trade-offs; executives want outcomes and risk; customers want value. For questions, repeat the question, answer concisely and check understanding. If you do not know, say so and follow up.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.body: Mistakes are normal. Pause, correct and continue. Do not apologise excessively. The audience does not know your script; a calm recovery often looks intentional.

workedExample.title: Five-minute CTO talk (illustrative)
workedExample.body: Message: reliability is a product feature. Story: an outage that cost a school day. Evidence: incident count and recovery time. Recommendation: invest in observability and runbooks. Close: ask the audience to adopt one reliability metric in their team.

misconceptions: Memorising a script word for word.
Speaking faster to fit more content.
Believing confidence is innate rather than practised.

build.business: CTOs represent technology to customers, staff and investors. Speaking skill affects trust and influence.
build.problem: Prepare and deliver a ten-minute technical talk to a mixed audience, with a recording and feedback loop.
requirements: Collect feedback from at least three people
Deliver the talk live or recorded
constraints: Must be completable in one week
build.design: Write a talk outline with message, sections and timing.
build.deliverable: Talk outline, slides, recording, feedback notes and Q&A log, referenced by path.
